payload.text:
I found it. The test fails because of the one commit on your branch, `9db8fa5` "Add a 15-minute session timeout to login". The test passes on `main` and fails on `feature/session-timeout`. I didn't change anything in the repo; I only ran the test against a temporary copy of `main` to confirm.

One thing doesn't match what you said: that commit is dated **Nov 2**, and your working tree has no uncommitted changes. So it's not something that changed since yesterday. Either you first ran the test after Nov 2, or whatever changed yesterday isn't in this checkout.

**Why it fails:** the commit changed `hash()` in `src/auth.js` but not the check inside `login()`, so the two now hash differently:
- `hash()` now trims the password and outputs **base64**. Dana's stored password is created with this version.
- `login()` checks against an inline hash that **doesn't trim** and outputs **hex**.

The two strings can never match, so even the correct password `correct horse` gets "wrong password". That's the assertion on line 4 of `test/login.test.js`.

**Fix:** have `login()` call `hash(password)` again, as it did on `main`. Then decide whether the switch to `.trim()` and base64 was on purpose. If you keep it, any password hashes you've already stored as hex will stop matching.

**Two other problems in the same commit:**
- `console.log('login attempt', username, password)` writes passwords in plain text to the logs. Remove it before this merges.
- `startSession` makes session IDs with `Math.random()`, which isn't secure for session tokens. Use `crypto.randomUUID()` or `crypto.randomBytes` instead.

I can make the fix if you want.
